Line 192-194 renders `By joining, you agree to our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.` as a plain non-interactive `<Text>` inside `Animated.View` — there is no `TouchableOpacity`, no `onPress`, and no `Linking.openURL` in the file. `grep -rniE "privacy|terms|eula" app/ src/ app.json` returns exactly this one line across the entire client. A reviewer tapping the words gets nothing. There is no Settings/About/Legal screen anywhere — app/(tabs)/profile/index.tsx has only Edit, Invite friends, Sign out.
consequence: Two distinct problems. (1) The user is asked to agree to two documents they have no way to read, which reviewers flag under 5.1.1(i) — the policy must be accessible, and for a UGC app the EULA/terms must be reachable. (2) 5.1.1(i) also requires the App Store Connect Privacy Policy URL to resolve to a real published policy; DEPLOYMENT.md:88-89 lists `/privacy` and `/terms` as still-unbuilt web routes, so at submission time the URL field will either be blank (metadata rejection) or point at a page with a literal `[DATE]` in the header. A reviewer who follows the URL and sees `**Effective date:** [DATE]` will reject the metadata regardless of the binary.
fix: Two changes. (a) app/(auth)/sign-up.tsx:192-194 — split the sentence and wrap each document name: `<Text onPress={() => Linking.openURL('https://whatsthemove.app/terms')} style={{color:'#FF6B35'}}>Terms of Service</Text>` and the same for `/privacy`; import `Linking` from react-native. (b) Add the same two links to app/(tabs)/profile/index.tsx beside the Sign out row so they remain reachable post-signup (Apple checks the logged-in state). (c) Replace `[DATE]` on line 3 of both docs/legal/*.md with a real date and publish them at the two URLs before filling the App Store Connect Privacy Policy URL field.
title: Privacy Policy and Terms exist as files but are unreachable from inside the app, and both carry an unfilled [DATE] placeholder

line: app.json plugins block, expo-location entry (`locationAlwaysAndWhenInUsePermission`); node_modules/@expo/config-plugins/build/ios/Permissions.js:34; node_modules/expo-location/plugin/build/withLocation.js:21-29; src/hooks/useLocation.ts:15
repro: Static trace of the config plugin. app.json passes only `locationAlwaysAndWhenInUsePermission` to expo-location. withLocation.js:21-24 calls `createPermissionsPlugin` with defaults for all three keys, including `NSLocationAlwaysUsageDescription: 'Allow $(PRODUCT_NAME) to access your location'`. Permissions.js:34 resolves each key as `permissions[k] || infoPlist[k] || description`. For `NSLocationAlwaysUsageDescription` the prop is undefined and app.json's `ios.infoPlist` does not set it, so the generic default is written into the built Info.plist verbatim. `NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription` gets "WTM uses your location to show moves near you." Meanwhile the only location call in the entire client is `Location.requestForegroundPermissionsAsync()` at useLocation.ts:15 — `grep -rn requestBackgroundPermissionsAsync app/ src/` returns nothing, and no background task, geofence, or `UIBackgroundModes: location` exists.
consequence: 5.1.1 rejection template: the binary declares persistent-location usage descriptions with no feature that requires persistent location. Compounding it, one of the two declared strings is Expo's untouched placeholder — "Allow What's The Move to access your location" states no purpose at all, which is precisely what 5.1.1's purpose-string requirement exists to catch. It also directly contradicts the app's own published policy: docs/legal/privacy-policy.md:25-26 lists "background location" under **What we do NOT collect**, and line 14-16 promises "We do **not** track location in the background." A reviewer comparing the Info.plist to the policy sees the binary asking for something the policy swears it never takes.
fix:
In app.json, replace the expo-location plugin entry with:
```json
["expo-location", {
  "locationWhenInUsePermission": "WTM uses your location to show moves happening near you.",
  "locationAlwaysAndWhenInUsePermission": false,
  "locationAlwaysPermission": false
}]
```
`false` is the documented sentinel — Permissions.js:30-32 deletes the key from the Info.plist rather than writing a default. That leaves exactly one location key, matching the one call in useLocation.ts and the policy text.
title: Build declares two persistent-location Info.plist keys — one with Expo's generic boilerplate string — for an app that only ever requests foreground location

line: app/_layout.tsx:15-21 (AuthGate calls useLocationInit() unconditionally in its body); src/hooks/useLocation.ts:9-11 (useEffect with empty deps → runs on first mount)
repro: Delete and reinstall, launch the app. `RootLayout` renders `AuthGate` (line 87). `AuthGate` calls `useLocationInit()` at line 21 in its component body, before any auth branch — the `useEffect(() => { requestLocation(); }, [])` at useLocation.ts:9-11 fires on the first render, in parallel with the `useEffect` at _layout.tsx:23 that has not yet routed anywhere. The system location dialog appears over the splash/welcome screen. app/(auth)/welcome.tsx contains no location copy at all (`grep -niE 'location|permission' app/(auth)/welcome.tsx` matches only a `locations={[0,0.5,1]}` gradient prop), so there is no priming screen explaining the ask.
consequence: 5.1.1 requires that data access be requested at the point it is needed and in context. A reviewer's first interaction with the build is a location prompt on a screen where they have not signed in, cannot see a map, and have no reason to grant it. Beyond the rejection risk, this is a measurable conversion cost: users who deny at cold launch are the ones you can never re-prompt without sending them to Settings, and the map tab (app/(tabs)/index.tsx) is the app's core surface. The prompt should fire when the map first needs coordinates, not before the account exists.
fix: Move the call out of the root. Delete `useLocationInit();` from app/_layout.tsx:21 and call it inside app/(tabs)/index.tsx (the map screen) instead, so it fires only after the auth + age gates have passed. Better still, gate it behind an in-app priming card on the map: render the map at the Pittsburgh default (`app/(tabs)/create.tsx:107-108` already uses 40.4406/-79.9959 as the fallback) with a "Show moves near me" button that calls `requestLocation()` on tap.
title: The iOS location prompt fires at cold launch, before the welcome screen, before the user has an account

line: supabase/migrations/019_profiles_exposure.sql:83-101 (move_chat_page has no blocked_either filter); src/components/moves/MoveChat.tsx:17-74 (MessageBubble renders no touchable); compare supabase/migrations/013_move_chat.sql:99, :152, :175 where blocked_either IS applied
repro: User A and user B both RSVP 'going' to the same move. A opens A's profile of B (app/user/[id].tsx), taps the ellipsis, Block user, confirms. `useBlockUser` (useSafety.ts:33-36) inserts the row; B's moves and spots vanish from A's feeds because `nearby_moves` (013:99, 011:121), `nearby_spots` (013:152) and `get_move_attendees` (013:175) all end with `and not public.blocked_either(...)`. A then opens the shared move (app/move/[id].tsx:283) and scrolls to the chat. `move_chat_page` at 019:83-101 filters only on move_id and on whether the caller is going/creator — there is no `blocked_either` clause — so every message B has posted is still rendered, with B's avatar and @username. Every new message B sends also arrives live: the realtime handler at useMoveChat.ts:55-91 appends any INSERT on `move_messages` for that move with no block check. From that screen A has no recourse: MessageBubble (MoveChat.tsx:17-74) is a plain `<View>` with no onPress, so tapping the avatar or username does nothing and there is no route from chat to the profile that carries the block/report menu.
consequence: Guideline 1.2 requires "a mechanism for users to block abusive users." The mechanism exists but stops at the one surface where harassment actually happens — a real-time group chat with people who have already agreed to meet at a physical location. A reviewer who tests block end-to-end (they do, for social apps) finds their blocked user still talking to them. Worse for the product than for the review: a user who blocks someone to escape harassment and then sees that person's messages keep arriving in the chat for a meetup they are both attending has been told the safety feature works when it does not. The block-confirm copy at app/user/[id].tsx:34 says "You won't see each other's moves, spots, or profiles" — technically accurate by omission, which is not a defence a reviewer accepts.
fix: Two changes. (a) In supabase/migrations/019_profiles_exposure.sql:99, add the filter that every other feed function already has — after the closing paren of the visibility `and (...)` block and before `order by`, insert `and not public.blocked_either(m.user_id)`. (b) Make the author tappable so block/report is reachable from chat: in MoveChat.tsx, wrap the avatar+username in `<TouchableOpacity onPress={() => router.push(`/user/${msg.user_id}`)}>` (import `useRouter` from expo-router), which lands on app/user/[id].tsx where the existing ellipsis menu at line 156-163 already provides both Block and Report. Note (a) alone still leaves the block one-directional in the RPC's `security definer` context — verify blocked_either resolves auth.uid() correctly there, as it does in the 013 functions.
title: Blocking a user does not hide their move-chat messages, and chat offers no path to block or report anyone

line: app.json ios.config.googleMapsApiKey = "$(GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY)" and android.config.googleMaps.apiKey = "$(GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY)"; app/(tabs)/index.tsx:3 and :146 (`provider={PROVIDER_GOOGLE}`)
repro: app.json is static JSON — Expo performs no environment interpolation on it (there is no app.config.js in the repo; `ls /home/user/wtm/wtm` shows app.json only). The string `$(GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY)` is written through verbatim: into Info.plist as `GMSApiKey` and into AndroidManifest as `com.google.android.geo.API_KEY`. On iOS, Xcode expands `$(VAR)` in Info.plist values against build settings; `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` is an EAS *environment variable* (DEPLOYMENT.md:79 sets it via `eas secret:create`), not an Xcode build setting, so it expands to empty. On Android there is no expansion mechanism at all and the literal string is passed to the Maps SDK. app/(tabs)/index.tsx:146 forces `provider={PROVIDER_GOOGLE}` on both platforms, so neither falls back to Apple Maps.
consequence: The default tab — the map that is the entire product — renders as a grey grid with a Google watermark and no tiles, with markers floating on nothing. Guideline 2.1 App Completeness: a reviewer who opens the app and sees the core screen not working rejects without reading further, and the rejection note will be a screenshot of a blank map. This also invalidates the screenshot set DEPLOYMENT.md:101 plans to capture ('map, spots layer, ...').
title: Google Maps API key is a literal placeholder string in app.json — the app's primary tab is a Google-provider map

line: docs/legal/privacy-policy.md:10-22 (the complete collection list); app/(auth)/verify-age.tsx:54-59 (writes birthdate to profiles); supabase/migrations/011_squad_safety.sql:10 (`birthdate date` column)
repro: Read docs/legal/privacy-policy.md:10-22 — the five bullets are Account info (email, username, display name, photo, bio), Location, Content you post, Invite graph, Device info (push token, diagnostics). Date of birth appears in none of them. Now trace app/(auth)/verify-age.tsx: line 54 computes `birthdateFor(selected, hadBirthday)` → a real date string, line 56-59 `supabase.from('profiles').update({ birthdate }).eq('id', profile.id)`. The value persists in `profiles.birthdate` (011:10) and drives the `set_age_range` trigger (011:17-34), which stores a derived `age_range` ('17-20' / '21-25') alongside it. The age gate is mandatory — app/_layout.tsx:42-45 routes any profile without a birthdate to verify-age and will not let them past.
consequence: 5.1.1(i) requires the privacy policy to "clearly and explicitly identify what data the app collects." Date of birth is a category Apple's own nutrition-label taxonomy calls out separately, and for a 17-25 app it is the single most sensitive field collected — it is the basis of the eligibility gate. A reviewer cross-checking the App Store Connect nutrition label against the linked policy finds a field the policy does not mention. Independently, DEPLOYMENT.md:102-103 plans the nutrition label as "location, user content, identifiers (push token)" — birthdate is missing there too, so the label will be filed inaccurate, which Apple treats as a metadata violation and can act on after approval.
fix: Add a bullet to docs/legal/privacy-policy.md after line 13: `- **Date of birth** — collected once at signup to enforce the 17-25 age requirement. We store the date and a derived age band; we do not use it for anything else.` Then add "Contact Info → Other User Contact Info / Sensitive Info" or, more precisely, the Date of Birth entry to the App Store Connect nutrition label, and amend the DEPLOYMENT.md:102-103 checklist line to match.
title: Privacy policy's "What we collect" list omits date of birth, which the app collects and stores

line: app.json plugins: ["expo-notifications", {...}]; supabase/functions/daily-digest/index.ts:88-101 (selects push_token, posts to Expo); supabase/migrations/002_auth_profiles.sql:8 (`push_token text`); no producer anywhere in app/ or src/
repro: `grep -rnE "getExpoPushTokenAsync|Notifications\.requestPermissionsAsync|getDevicePushTokenAsync" app/ src/` returns zero. `grep -rn push_token app/ src/` returns only the two type declarations (src/types/database.ts:24, src/types/app.ts:23) — no read, no write. The only write grant exists (015_security_hardening.sql:42 grants update on push_token) but nothing exercises it. daily-digest/index.ts:88-89 then runs `.select('push_token, username').not('push_token','is',null)` and line 101 sends `to: u.push_token`. Because nothing ever populates the column, that filter matches zero rows on every run.
consequence: Three concrete costs. (1) The daily digest — the retention mechanism DEPLOYMENT.md treats as shipped — sends nothing, forever, silently. (2) The app declares the expo-notifications plugin, which adds the `aps-environment` entitlement and a push capability to a binary with no notification feature; reviewers do ask what the push capability is for. (3) docs/legal/privacy-policy.md:21 tells users the app collects "a push notification token (if you enable notifications)" and there is no enable path, and DEPLOYMENT.md:102-103 plans to declare "identifiers (push token)" on the nutrition label — declaring collection of data the binary never collects is the inverse of the usual label error but still an inaccurate label.
fix: Either implement or remove — do not ship the half. To implement: in app/_layout.tsx, after the profile exists (inside the AuthGate effect, after line 45), call `const { status } = await Notifications.requestPermissionsAsync(); if (status === 'granted') { const t = (await Notifications.getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId })).data; await supabase.from('profiles').update({ push_token: t }).eq('id', profile.id); }` — note this must be a user-visible opt-in, not silent, and `projectId` requires fixing the placeholder in app.json's extra.eas block. To remove: delete the expo-notifications plugin entry from app.json, delete supabase/functions/daily-digest, and drop the push_token bullet from privacy-policy.md:21 and the nutrition-label line in DEPLOYMENT.md:103.
title: Push notification stack is declared and consumed server-side but no client code ever obtains a token — push_token is永 null

file: app.json ios.infoPlist.NSCameraUsageDescription and android.permissions["CAMERA"]; the three image entry points are app/(tabs)/create.tsx
line: app.json ios.infoPlist.NSCameraUsageDescription and android.permissions["CAMERA"]; the three image entry points are app/(tabs)/create.tsx:84-94, app/(tabs)/profile/edit.tsx:22, app/add-spot.tsx:37 — all `launchImageLibraryAsync`
repro: `grep -rnE "launchCameraAsync|requestCameraPermissionsAsync" app/ src/` returns zero hits. All three image flows call `ImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync` only, which needs NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription and nothing else. app.json nonetheless declares `NSCameraUsageDescription: "WTM needs camera access to take a photo for your move."` and lists `CAMERA` in android.permissions; separately, node_modules/expo-image-picker/plugin/build/withImagePicker.js:26-32 would default-fill NSCameraUsageDescription anyway since `cameraPermission` is not passed. There is also no UI affordance offering "Take a photo" — pickImage in create.tsx:84 goes straight to the library with no action sheet.
consequence: Apple's automated purpose-string check does not reject for a declared-but-unfired string, so the iOS rejection probability here is genuinely low — I am reporting it because it is provable and cheap, not because it will bounce the build. The real exposure is Google Play, where a declared CAMERA permission with no camera feature draws a policy flag, as does READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE / WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE in the same android.permissions array (both are obsolete on API 33+ and expo-image-picker does not need them).
fix: In app.json: delete the `NSCameraUsageDescription` line from ios.infoPlist, and pass `"cameraPermission": false` in the expo-image-picker plugin options so withImagePicker does not write its default back in. Trim android.permissions to `["ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION", "ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION"]` — CAMERA, READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE are all unused. Alternatively, if a camera capture flow is intended, add an action sheet to pickImage offering `launchCameraAsync`, which makes all three declarations legitimate.
title: Camera permission declared on both platforms; no code path ever opens the camera

line: app.json extra.eas.projectId = "YOUR_EAS_PROJECT_ID"; eas.json submit.production.ios appleId = "YOUR_APPLE_ID", ascAppId = "YOUR_APP_STORE_CONNECT_APP_ID", appleTeamId = "YOUR_APPLE_TEAM_ID"; eas.json submit.production.android serviceAccountKeyPath = "./secrets/google-service-account.json"
repro: Run `eas build --platform ios --profile production`. The CLI resolves `extra.eas.projectId` and fails on the literal `YOUR_EAS_PROJECT_ID`, which is not a UUID. If that is fixed, `eas submit --profile production` then fails resolving `YOUR_APPLE_ID`. `ls /home/user/wtm/wtm/secrets` — the directory does not exist, so the Android service-account path is dangling too.
consequence: Not a guideline rejection — it is a blocker that fires before a reviewer ever sees the binary, and it sits underneath every other finding in this report. Also worth noting alongside it: this app is invite-gated (app/(auth)/invite.tsx, validated by supabase/functions/validate-invite), so a reviewer who reaches the build and has no working invite code is stopped at the second screen. DEPLOYMENT.md:106-107 already flags this correctly ("include a working invite code for the review team") — that note must actually make it into the App Review Information field, or Guideline 2.1 rejects for an inaccessible app.
fix: Replace `YOUR_EAS_PROJECT_ID` in app.json with the UUID from `eas init`; fill the three ios fields in eas.json's submit.production from App Store Connect; either create ./secrets/google-service-account.json (gitignored) or drop the android submit block until Play submission is in scope. Before submitting, generate a permanent unlimited-use invite code and paste it plus a test account into App Store Connect → App Review Information → Notes.
title: Submission identifiers in app.json and eas.json are unreplaced template placeholders — the build/submit pipeline cannot run

line: supabase/migrations/015_security_hardening.sql:87 (insert into public.profiles (id, username, invited_by)) vs. app/(auth)/sign-up.tsx:72 and supabase/migrations/007_referrals.sql:67-71
repro: Open /(auth)/sign-up, fill Username "bigmike", Display name "Big Mike", email, password, tap "Let's go". supabase.auth.signUp sends options.data.display_name = "Big Mike". The on_auth_user_created trigger runs the LAST definition of handle_new_user, which is 015's (015 supersedes 007's, which did read raw_user_meta_data->>'display_name'). 015's INSERT names only (id, username, invited_by).
consequence: profiles.display_name is NULL for every account created after 015 applies. Every render site is written as `display_name || username`, so the entire app falls back to the raw handle: profile header (app/(tabs)/profile/index.tsx:88), other people's profiles (app/user/[id].tsx:180), the attendee list (app/move/[id]/attendees.tsx:57), chat author initials (MoveChat.tsx:19), avatar initials everywhere. The "Display name" field on the signup form is a dead input — a teen types their name, taps through, and the app never shows it. Only fixable afterwards via Edit Profile, which most users never open. This hits 100% of new users, on day one.
fix: In supabase/migrations/015_security_hardening.sql:87, restore the column: `insert into public.profiles (id, username, display_name, invited_by) values (new.id, coalesce(new.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'username', 'member_' || left(new.id::text, 8)), nullif(trim(coalesce(new.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'display_name', '')), ''), v_inviter);` — ship it as migration 021 rather than editing 015 if 015 has already been applied anywhere.
title: Display name typed at sign-up is silently thrown away — handle_new_user stopped inserting it

line: supabase/migrations/016_one_nearby_moves.sql:131 (order by m.hot_score desc, m.starts_at asc) + supabase/migrations/012_activity_momentum.sql:20,28-32 (recalc_hot_score) + src/hooks/useCreateMove.ts:38-42 (creator auto-RSVP)
repro: With an account older than 24h (011:126 cooldown), open the Create tab. Title anything, pick a category, type a location, set the start time to 15 minutes from now, toggle "Limit spots" on and set it to 1, tap "Post it". useCreateMove inserts an rsvps row for the creator (line 38), which fires rsvp_hot_score -> recalc_hot_score. v_hours = greatest(0.25, 0.25) = 0.25, v_count = 1, v_cap = 1, so hot_score = 1/0.25 * (1 + 1/1) = 8.0. Repeat 20 times — nothing in the schema rate-limits move creation past the one-time 24h new-account cooldown, and moves_authenticated_insert / moves_insert only check creator_id = auth.uid().
consequence: A real move 6 hours out with 20 of 30 spots filled scores 20/6 * (1 + 20/30) = 5.6 and loses to a fake move with one attendee. Twenty junk posts own the entire first page of nearby_moves for every user within the 8047 m radius. Without the capacity cap the same move scores 1/0.25 = 4.0, which clears MoveCard.tsx:38 HOT_THRESHOLD = 1.5, so it also renders the "🔥 Trending" badge on a move with literally one person going. This is free top-of-feed placement for anyone bored enough to tap Post twenty times, in the one surface the whole product depends on.
fix: In 012_activity_momentum.sql, damp the imminence term and require real signal: at line 20 raise the floor from 0.25 to 2.0 (`greatest(2.0, extract(epoch from (m.starts_at - now())) / 3600.0)`) so a 15-minute-out move is not worth 4x, and at line 29 subtract the creator's own RSVP (`greatest(0, v_count - 1)::numeric / v_hours`) so a self-RSVP scores zero. Separately add a per-creator creation limit as a RESTRICTIVE insert policy on moves: `(select count(*) from public.moves where creator_id = auth.uid() and created_at > now() - interval '1 hour') < 5`.
title: hot_score is the feed's sort key and one self-RSVP on a soon-starting move beats every genuinely popular move

line: app/(tabs)/profile/edit.tsx:126 (TextInput, no maxLength) and :47 (update display_name) + supabase/migrations/002_auth_profiles.sql:4-5 (display_name text, bio text — no constraint) + supabase/migrations/015_security_hardening.sql:42 (grant update (display_name, ..., bio, ...)) vs. 015:189-193 (moves/spots description capped at 2000)
repro: Copy a large block of text (a full Wikipedia article, a pasted log — anything from another app's clipboard). Profile tab -> Edit -> long-press the DISPLAY NAME field -> Paste -> Save. The bio field below it is capped at maxLength={150} (edit.tsx:166) and moves.description is capped at 2000 chars by 015:190, but the display-name field has no maxLength prop and profiles.display_name has no CHECK constraint in any of the 21 migrations. The column is explicitly UPDATE-grantable at 015:42.
consequence: Two outcomes. (a) Storage: the exact hole 015:186-193 closed for moves.description ("a member could store a 100 MB description and fill the 500 MB free-tier database from inside the app") is still wide open on profiles.display_name and profiles.bio, and unlike descriptions it is reachable with one paste and no API access. It also feeds profiles_display_name_trgm, a GIN trigram index (002:56), so each megabyte of name explodes into ~1M index entries. (b) Layout: even 4,000 characters is enough — the name renders at fontSize 22 with NO numberOfLines at app/(tabs)/profile/index.tsx:88 and app/user/[id].tsx:180, and at fontSize 15 with no numberOfLines inside a FlatList row at app/move/[id]/attendees.tsx:57. The bio, stats card, invite card and "My moves" section are pushed thousands of points down the ScrollView; the attendee list becomes one row per screen. Anyone can do this to their own row and it is visible to every other user who opens the attendee list of a shared move.
fix: Add the constraint (new migration 021): `alter table public.profiles add constraint profiles_display_name_len check (display_name is null or char_length(display_name) <= 40); alter table public.profiles add constraint profiles_bio_len check (bio is null or char_length(bio) <= 300);` Add `maxLength={40}` to the TextInput at app/(tabs)/profile/edit.tsx:126 and to the Display name Field at app/(auth)/sign-up.tsx:143. Add `numberOfLines={1}` to the three name <Text> elements at profile/index.tsx:88, user/[id].tsx:180, attendees.tsx:57.
title: display_name and bio have no length ceiling in the DB and no maxLength on the display-name input — 015 capped descriptions for exactly this reason and missed profiles

line: app/(tabs)/create.tsx:112 (parseInt(form.maxAttendees)), :322 (digit-strip), :129 (Alert with err.message) + supabase/migrations/004_moves.sql:34 (max_attendees_positive)
repro: Two inputs, same field. (a) Create tab -> Capacity -> toggle "Limit spots" on -> the field prefills "10" -> backspace twice -> type "0" -> tap "Post it". create.tsx:112 evaluates parseInt("0") = 0, useCreateMove sends max_attendees: 0, and 004:34 `check (max_attendees is null or max_attendees > 0)` rejects it. create.tsx:129 renders err.message verbatim. (b) Same path but backspace to empty and leave it empty -> parseInt("") = NaN -> `NaN ?? null` is NaN (?? only catches null/undefined) -> supabase-js JSON-serialises it, and JSON.stringify(NaN) is null -> the row is inserted with max_attendees = NULL. (c) Type "9999999999" (no maxLength on the field) -> exceeds int4 -> "value \"9999999999\" is out of range for type integer".
consequence: (a) and (c): the teen sees an Alert titled "Error" reading `new row for relation "moves" violates check constraint "max_attendees_positive"` — a database internals dump as the only feedback, with no hint that the problem is the number they typed. The move is not created and no field is marked. (b) is worse because it is silent: the user explicitly turned "Limit spots" ON, cleared the box, and gets a move with NO cap. moves_with_counts computes spots_left = NULL and is_full = false, MoveCard.tsx:41 sets fillPct = null so the capacity bar never renders, move/[id].tsx:194 hides the "N / M going" card entirely, check_move_capacity (005:29) returns early on NULL, and the waitlist can never engage. A party the host meant to cap at 10 accepts 400 RSVPs and the host has no way to tell why.
